text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Most Bosnian refugees living abroad were not able to vote in the September 14 elections due to badly organized polling, Bosnian Prime Minister Hasan Muratovic tells a press conference on Thursday.
- Curfew in Bosnia will last as long as it is needed because it is in interest of citizens' security, Bosnian Federation Minister of Interior says in an interview.
- A Bosnian power equipment producer clinched a $59 million deal with Libiya to draft, produce and install a 847 kilometer power line, a company official said on Thursday.

- The director of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) which is responsible for election irregularities says he has been asked not to certify the results by the International Crisis Group, a non-governmental organisation.
